sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Best guide and build for Nekomata from ZZZ (Zenless Zone Zero). Nekomata is an rank character with the Physical attribute who belongs to the Attack Specialty and who is part of the Cunning Hares faction.
 "The best mackerel is always the one you haven't eaten yet~" — Nekomiya Mana. Spirited and mischievous, she likes to play tricks on others. Your wallet is her wallet. (Really... It's hers now.) Athletic and daring, no Hollow is too dangerous for her. "Cats love fish" is actually an incorrect stereotype. But Nekomata does love fish... She's seen a lot of cat-astrophy and "curiosity killed the cat" moments, and seen many a secret that can't be told.

sections.text: This tier list assesses Agents (characters) based on their combat potential in Zenless Zone Zero's most demanding contents - Deadly Assault (DA) and Shiyu Defense (SD) . Please keep in mind Zenless Zone Zero is a skill-based game and each character has a different playstyle, difficulty level and even special tricks and combos. Zenless Zone Zero is also a team based game and it's only by combining both these factors to the highest level a character can reach optimal performance.

sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Low-cost EX Special grants her a niche in Seed teams as a Steel Charge funnel.

sections.heading: Cons

Some of the lowest personal damage potential of any DPS in the entire game..

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: Nekomata is an S-rank Physical Attack Agent who specializes in executing low-damage but very swift attacks as her primary means of dealing damage to enemies. As a damage dealer, she provides no supportive capabilities in her own kit, but with the recent addition of agents like Seed she has become better than ever, even if she mainly takes on the role of a support in Seed Teams. Let’s delve into the specifics of her kit:

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
sections.text:
Nekomata is one of the simplest characters in the game with very few intricacies. However, one of them is contained within her Core Passive effect, which allows her to gain a significant, but short-term damage boost after executing a Dodge Counter or Quick Assist. To be exact, the buff goes as high as 60% general DMG Bonus for 6s.
 As a result, due to the short duration of this buff, Nekomata likes playing in teams that offer speedy access to Quick Assists during stun (this means Astra/Nicole) and she also enjoys staying actively on-field, dodging enemy attacks. It is key to maximize Nekomata’s damage output to ensure uptime on this buff on all of her highest damage abilities (being her Ultimate, EX Special and even her Chain Attack if possible). Nonetheless, the uptime on this buff is very short so it can be difficult to play around over the course of lengthier combos — but with agents who can provide near-instant access to Quick Assists like Astra Yao and Nicole, it isn’t impossible.
 Via her Additional Ability, Nekomata could gain an extra 35% DMG boost to the next EX Special that follows an Assault Anomaly trigger, stackable up to 2 times. Unfortunately however, none of her teams apply enough anomaly for this to ever work out, which makes her additional ability pretty useless. Hence, in her best teams, this Additional Ability effect can and should be safely skipped out on without much issue.

sections.heading: EX Special
sections.text: Nekomata’s EX Special is a low 40 Energy cost. This is one of the lowest cost EX Specials in the game and it deals only an okay amount of damage as a drawback to its low cost. In addition, the animation is rather slow compared to the rest of her kit, but Nekomata can be switched out of this animation on cast in order to mitigate this effect.

sections.heading: Basic Attack
sections.text:
Nekomata’s Basic Attack has 2 different mechanics: Her 5-part Basic Attack has a special mechanic on the 5th hit that allows it to repeat up to 3 times with a 1 in 3 chance. This same mechanic also exists on her Crimson Blade attack triggered by holding Basic Attack during any of the first 3 hits. It essentially acts as a weaker version of her Basic Attack 5 which means it’s not worth executing over her regular Basic Attack string.
 Additionally, these potential extra hits may not always be desirable depending on your W-Engine choice. Nekomata’s Steel Cushion W-Engine, one of her top choices, provides extra damage when dealing damage to enemies from behind. These extra hits will have you bounce back and forth between the enemy’s front and back which can prove problematic if trying to capitalize on this W-Engine’s effect.

sections.heading: Unused/Redundant parts of her kit
sections.text: All of Nekomata’s Dodge and Assist-related moves work as you’d expect them to so we won’t go in detail over them. However, don’t forget about maximizing on her Core Passive’s DMG buff via her Dodge Counter and Quick Assist.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
sections.text:
In the current meta, Nekomata is in a rather difficult spot. Her damage has always been on the low end since her release, and stronger and stronger characters releasing over time did not help her stand out much. That is, until Seed came around.
 With Seed’s release, Nekomata’s low-cost EX Special came to light once again, since Seed’s Steel Charge mechanic which allows her to unleash a lot of her damage can be replenished by expending Energy as the active Agent. Nekomata does this pretty well, and since her damage has become significantly overshadowed by every DPS Agent since Nekomata’s initial release, she tends to run supportive Disk Drives and W-Engine builds, but her potential to funnel Steel Charge to Seed is rather appreciated and a good F2P alternative to her teams. This is Nekomata’s only current meta position, but she is still overshadowed in this team by other, better premium options or Corin.
 We can conclude Nekomata is rather replaceable in the meta, yet does hold some niche use cases for Proxies who want to make use of her.

sections.heading: Synergy
sections.text:
Below we list only the most important synergies for Nekomata . The character can work with others if you know what to do and how to use them.

 Dialyn - Dialyn is easily the best Stunner for Nekomata and far surpasses any double support comps at the time of her release. Her strong all-around buffs are good as is, but the Ultimate conversion she offers is particularly great, given that Nekomata's damage is loaded on EXs, Chains and Ultimates. As Dialyn is a Physical Agent, she both enables Nekomata's Additional Ability (despite its limited value add) and simultaneously contributes to its activation through Physical Anomaly build-up. When paired with a fast time-to-stun and Nekomata's accessible burst, she's the most optimal choice.
 Seed - Nekomata's only real use case is in Seed teams as an Energy battery. Her low-cost EX Special with the possibility to run a W-Engine like Housekeeper and a supportive set like Astral Voice makes her a good Support to boost Seed's damage, where her main role will be to funnel Steel Charge via frequent EX Specials so that Seed can shine and deal good damage on her own.
 Trigger Pulchra - When played with the intent to deal damage Nekomata highly values her fieldtime and stun windows something both Pulchra and Trigger provide thanks to their ability to inflict daze and their buffs without soaking up too much of it.
 Astra Yao Nicole - Astra provides an easy access to quick assists even during stun windows and due to the short duration of Nekomata's self-buff and her inability to self-access quick assists and dodge counters during the enemy stun window, Astra is one of the better choices for Nekomata, allowing her to maintain her core passive even during stuns. Nekomata also pairs extremely well with DEF Shred sources such as Trigger or Cordis Germina and with DEF Shred Stacking being a valuable choice for a substantial damage increase, Nicole can do extremely well as well. Nicole can also provide up to 15% crit rate at Mindscape 6 in addition to yet again easy access to quick assists by her EX Special, Ultimate and Chain Attacks.

 Review
 Nekomata is an S-rank Physical Attack Agent who specializes in executing low-damage but very swift attacks as her primary means of dealing damage to enemies. As a damage dealer, she provides no supportive capabilities in her own kit, but with the recent addition of agents like Seed she has become better than ever, even if she mainly takes on the role of a support in Seed Teams. Let’s delve into the specifics of her kit:
 Key Mechanics
 Nekomata is one of the simplest characters in the game with very few intricacies. However, one of them is contained within her Core Passive effect, which allows her to gain a significant, but short-term damage boost after executing a Dodge Counter or Quick Assist. To be exact, the buff goes as high as 60% general DMG Bonus for 6s.
 As a result, due to the short duration of this buff, Nekomata likes playing in teams that offer speedy access to Quick Assists during stun (this means Astra/Nicole) and she also enjoys staying actively on-field, dodging enemy attacks. It is key to maximize Nekomata’s damage output to ensure uptime on this buff on all of her highest damage abilities (being her Ultimate, EX Special and even her Chain Attack if possible). Nonetheless, the uptime on this buff is very short so it can be difficult to play around over the course of lengthier combos — but with agents who can provide near-instant access to Quick Assists like Astra Yao and Nicole, it isn’t impossible.
 Via her Additional Ability, Nekomata could gain an extra 35% DMG boost to the next EX Special that follows an Assault Anomaly trigger, stackable up to 2 times. Unfortunately however, none of her teams apply enough anomaly for this to ever work out, which makes her additional ability pretty useless. Hence, in her best teams, this Additional Ability effect can and should be safely skipped out on without much issue.
 EX Special
 Nekomata’s EX Special is a low 40 Energy cost. This is one of the lowest cost EX Specials in the game and it deals only an okay amount of damage as a drawback to its low cost. In addition, the animation is rather slow compared to the rest of her kit, but Nekomata can be switched out of this animation on cast in order to mitigate this effect.
 Basic Attack
 Nekomata’s Basic Attack has 2 different mechanics: Her 5-part Basic Attack has a special mechanic on the 5th hit that allows it to repeat up to 3 times with a 1 in 3 chance. This same mechanic also exists on her Crimson Blade attack triggered by holding Basic Attack during any of the first 3 hits. It essentially acts as a weaker version of her Basic Attack 5 which means it’s not worth executing over her regular Basic Attack string.
 Additionally, these potential extra hits may not always be desirable depending on your W-Engine choice. Nekomata’s Steel Cushion W-Engine, one of her top choices, provides extra damage when dealing damage to enemies from behind. These extra hits will have you bounce back and forth between the enemy’s front and back which can prove problematic if trying to capitalize on this W-Engine’s effect.
 Unused/Redundant parts of her kit
 All of Nekomata’s Dodge and Assist-related moves work as you’d expect them to so we won’t go in detail over them. However, don’t forget about maximizing on her Core Passive’s DMG buff via her Dodge Counter and Quick Assist.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 In the current meta, Nekomata is in a rather difficult spot. Her damage has always been on the low end since her release, and stronger and stronger characters releasing over time did not help her stand out much. That is, until Seed came around.
 With Seed’s release, Nekomata’s low-cost EX Special came to light once again, since Seed’s Steel Charge mechanic which allows her to unleash a lot of her damage can be replenished by expending Energy as the active Agent. Nekomata does this pretty well, and since her damage has become significantly overshadowed by every DPS Agent since Nekomata’s initial release, she tends to run supportive Disk Drives and W-Engine builds, but her potential to funnel Steel Charge to Seed is rather appreciated and a good F2P alternative to her teams. This is Nekomata’s only current meta position, but she is still overshadowed in this team by other, better premium options or Corin.
 We can conclude Nekomata is rather replaceable in the meta, yet does hold some niche use cases for Proxies who want to make use of her.

 Teams & Synergy

 Synergy
 Below we list only the most important synergies for Nekomata . The character can work with others if you know what to do and how to use them.

 Dialyn - Dialyn is easily the best Stunner for Nekomata and far surpasses any double support comps at the time of her release. Her strong all-around buffs are good as is, but the Ultimate conversion she offers is particularly great, given that Nekomata's damage is loaded on EXs, Chains and Ultimates. As Dialyn is a Physical Agent, she both enables Nekomata's Additional Ability (despite its limited value add) and simultaneously contributes to its activation through Physical Anomaly build-up. When paired with a fast time-to-stun and Nekomata's accessible burst, she's the most optimal choice.
 Seed - Nekomata's only real use case is in Seed teams as an Energy battery. Her low-cost EX Special with the possibility to run a W-Engine like Housekeeper and a supportive set like Astral Voice makes her a good Support to boost Seed's damage, where her main role will be to funnel Steel Charge via frequent EX Specials so that Seed can shine and deal good damage on her own.
 Trigger Pulchra - When played with the intent to deal damage Nekomata highly values her fieldtime and stun windows something both Pulchra and Trigger provide thanks to their ability to inflict daze and their buffs without soaking up too much of it.
 Astra Yao Nicole - Astra provides an easy access to quick assists even during stun windows and due to the short duration of Nekomata's self-buff and her inability to self-access quick assists and dodge counters during the enemy stun window, Astra is one of the better choices for Nekomata, allowing her to maintain her core passive even during stuns. Nekomata also pairs extremely well with DEF Shred sources such as Trigger or Cordis Germina and with DEF Shred Stacking being a valuable choice for a substantial damage increase, Nicole can do extremely well as well. Nicole can also provide up to 15% crit rate at Mindscape 6 in addition to yet again easy access to quick assists by her EX Special, Ultimate and Chain Attacks.
